title: Unearthing Critical Security Flaws in Check Processing Systems
rule_cited: §1 stratified (third-party evaluator) + §2 all three tests pass — evaluator-asserted, evidence-backed, independently codeable empirical model finding
reason: Robust Intelligence reports its own black-box adversarial attack (SCAR) succeeding against deployed commercial check-processing recognition models, with a concrete demonstrated misread ($401 read as $701); vendors are anonymised, which caps it at Tier B under §4.

findings.finding: Robust Intelligence's SCAR black-box attack flipped a small number of pixels in binarized check images and caused deployed commercial check-processing systems to misread the amount, simultaneously fooling the paired CAR and LAR amount-recognition models into the same wrong amount (a $401 check read as $701).
findings.finding_quote: For example, flipping the pixels shown in red below caused an industry-standard check processing system to recognize a $701 transaction from a check made out for just $401
findings.models_systems: Commercial automated check-processing systems (paired CAR and LAR amount-recognition models) licensed from unnamed "industry-leading providers" serving major US banks
findings.tier_reasoning: Gate 1 passes — this is an empirical model finding: a measured attack success against real deployed models, not a framework or governance write-up. Gate 2 fails — the targets are identified only as "software licensed from industry-leading providers", so no company or model is named and no specific company response could reasonably be expected; per §4 that sends it to TIER B. Against the three Tier A conditions: (1) PASSES (empirical model finding); (2) FAILS — anonymised targets explicitly fail this condition; (3) would pass on concerningness (a security bypass with direct financial-fraud consequence, not a reassuring null or a benchmark score) but is moot once (2) fails.
findings.finding_type: third-party adversarial/red-team evaluation (vendor blog reporting the evaluator's own research)
findings.access_type: Black-box (report states SCAR "assumes no knowledge about the internal workings of the AI system it attacks; the only information it receives from the model is the final prediction")
